run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: In production-us-east-2 the checkout-service 500s are preceded by, and textually attributed to, a payment-provider timeout: checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 2026-11-23T16:00:56Z, while production-us-east-2 payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at the same second, and checkout-service then logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 17:00:56Z and 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' at 17:30:56Z. That is the only log evidence in the app-269-prod-logs index (6 documents total, 4 of them production-us-east-2 ERROR records). The deepest observable cause is therefore payment-service's calls to its stripe-us payment provider timing out at 30s, which then trips checkout-service's circuit breaker; the provider endpoint itself is not observable in any available source, so the ultimate trigger is unresolved. Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query, and Kubernetes access is limited to the production-eu-west-2 cluster, so no error-rate, latency, trace or pod-level evidence for production-us-east-2 was available. The production-eu-west-2 cluster (including a just-created app-269 Deployment checkout-service running nginx:1.27-alpine) is a different cluster with different workloads and cannot be tied to these 500s; its same-named services logged healthy INFO lines. All fault-injection flags in the reachable cluster's flagd-config (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) are 'off', which rules that mechanism out for the cluster I can see but says nothing about production-us-east-2.

claims.text: app-269-prod-logs is the only log index in the Elasticsearch source and holds 6 documents (7.3kb); its mapped fields are cluster, level, message, service and timestamp (no @timestamp).

Querying app-269-prod-logs over the full authorized window returned all 6 documents: 4 cluster=production-us-east-2 ERROR records for checkout-service/payment-service between 2026-11-23T16:00:56Z and 2026-11-23T17:30:56Z, and 2 cluster=production-eu-west-2 INFO records at 16:00:56Z and 17:30:56Z.
In production-us-east-2, checkout-service logged at 2026-11-23T16:00:56Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' (level ERROR).

In production-us-east-2, payment-service logged at 2026-11-23T16:00:56Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' (level ERROR) — the payment-service's own record of its outbound charge call to stripe-us timing out.

In production-us-east-2, checkout-service logged at 2026-11-23T17:00:56Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)', and at 2026-11-23T17:30:56Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' — checkout-service itself rejecting requests because of accumulated payment-service failures.

The same-named services in the other cluster, production-eu-west-2, produced no error records at these timestamps: checkout-service logged 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 2026-11-23T16:00:56Z and payment-service logged 'Adyen-eu healthy' at 2026-11-23T17:30:56Z. These are different cluster-scoped entities, so they neither confirm nor contradict the production-us-east-2 failure.

In the reachable cluster (production-eu-west-2) namespace app-269 there is a Deployment checkout-service created 2026-11-23T18:00:54Z, generation 1, 1/1 ready, container image nginx:1.27-alpine with cpu 10m/memory 16Mi requests; it owns ReplicaSet checkout-service-6d7f474c45, which owns Running/Ready pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-gkw69 with restartCount 0. No Service and no NetworkPolicy objects exist in namespace app-269.

Events in the reachable cluster are limited to namespace app-269 around 2026-11-23T18:00:54Z–18:00:56Z: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started (1 each). These are rollout events for the nginx-based app-269 checkout-service, and the pod's logs show only nginx startup lines (no request or 500 entries).

The flagd-config ConfigMap in namespace otel-demo of the reachable production-eu-west-2 cluster defines fault-injection flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), both with state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off' (as do all other listed flags: adFailure, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, etc.).

Application logs of the production-eu-west-2 otel-demo checkout pod (checkout-6578865d87-v6flf) between 15:30Z and 18:01Z contained one line matching error keywords, and it was an INFO line: 'order confirmation email sent to "reed@example.com"' at 2026-11-23T16:23:06Z.

The production-us-east-2 checkout-service 500s are a consequence of payment-service failing its calls to the stripe-us provider: payment-service's /v1/charges call to stripe-us exceeded 30s, payment-service therefore returned failures (checkout measured a 41% failure rate), and checkout-service's circuit breaker for payment-service opened, so /api/checkout requests are rejected with errors. This fits the exact wording and 30s duration in both independent log lines and the one-hour sequence in which they occur.

The deepest cause lies beyond payment-service at the stripe-us payment-provider endpoint or on the payment-service to stripe-us path (provider latency/outage or egress/DNS/timeout misconfiguration). This is not verified: no metric, trace, pod or provider-side data for production-us-east-2 or for stripe-us was obtainable in this Run.

Fault injection through the reachable cluster's flagd flags (paymentFailure / paymentUnreachable) is rejected as the cause of these 500s: both flags resolve to defaultVariant 'off' in flagd-config, and that ConfigMap belongs to the production-eu-west-2 otel-demo namespace, not to production-us-east-2 where the errors were logged.

The app-269 Kubernetes Deployment checkout-service visible to me (nginx:1.27-alpine, created 2026-11-23T18:00:54Z) is not the checkout-service producing the production-us-east-2 500s: it runs in the reachable production-eu-west-2 cluster, its container is stock nginx, its pod restarted 0 times and is Ready, and its logs contain only nginx startup output with no failing checkout requests.

Mitigate at payment-service's stripe-us integration: check stripe-us provider status/latency and the payment-service egress path (DNS, proxy, TLS), and review the 30s client timeout, retry and circuit-breaker thresholds; the 30s timeout both in checkout's and payment-service's messages makes provider-side latency the first thing to test.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger availability for this investigation target and obtain Kubernetes access to production-us-east-2, so error rate, latency percentiles, trace-level payment→stripe spans, and payment-service pod/config state can be checked rather than inferred from four log lines.

gaps: Prometheus (registered target m0-otel-20260909) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for get_all_labels, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query; no error-rate, latency, pod container-info or target-health series could be read, so the onset time, pre-incident baseline and current state of checkout-service/payment-service are unknown.

Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for traces_list_services and traces_search(service=payment); no trace data exists in this Run, so the checkout→payment→stripe call edges are inferred only from log text, not from parent references.

Kubernetes access covers only the production-eu-west-2 cluster; no pod, deployment, event, ConfigMap or NetworkPolicy objects for production-us-east-2 (the cluster named in the question) could be read, so payment-service/client timeout configuration, pod restarts and endpoint wiring there are unknown.

app-269-prod-logs contains only 6 documents (4 for production-us-east-2) sampled at 16:00:56Z, 17:00:56Z and 17:30:56Z; there is no log coverage between those instants, before 16:00:56Z or after 17:30:56Z, so when the stripe-us timeouts began and whether they persist is unknown.
No stripe-us provider telemetry, status or logs are available in any registered source; the ultimate trigger of the 30s timeouts is unobserved.
Secrets cannot be read; any provider credentials or timeout settings held in Secrets for production-us-east-2 could not be verified.

The error-filtered log query on the production-eu-west-2 payment pod (payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm) returned no matching lines (status no_data; 474 of 478 read lines filtered out); that is an empty query result, not proof that nothing was logged there.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no change/deployment record for production-us-east-2 payment-service or checkout-service around 16:00Z could be checked.
next_steps: Check stripe-us provider status/incident page and measure latency from production-us-east-2 to stripe-us /v1/charges.
Once Prometheus is reachable, compare checkout-service and payment-service error-rate/latency series over 2026-11-23T14:00Z–18:01Z against an earlier baseline to fix the deviation onset.
Inspect production-us-east-2 payment-service and checkout-service pod logs, container termination reasons and any ConfigMap holding stripe client timeouts/retry and circuit-breaker settings.
If traces become available, confirm the checkout→payment→stripe-us span chain and which span carries the timeout error.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
